father_candidate.claim: John of Glenleslie remains an unselected father candidate for the Glenleslie Robert, 18%.
father_candidate.basis: John Glasgow-1022 is an unselected father candidate for the Glenleslie Robert represented within Glasgow-1367, assessed at 18% subjective confidence. The 1851 transcription places Antrim-born Glasgow farmers John, reported 99, and Robert, 72, in Glenleslie houses 21 and 23, with the Hamill household between them. Their approximately 27-year age gap fits fatherhood better than an ordinary sibling interval. However, the transcription defines field 17 as the year of first marriage and gives John 1791. Robert’s census-implied birth about 1778–1779 precedes that by roughly twelve years. Earlier fatherhood would therefore require nonmarital fatherhood, incomplete reporting or a wrong age/date; none is established. Locality, surname, farming and generation also fit collateral kin. John remains the leading named local father comparison, while an unidentified father is more likely overall.

father_candidate.record_scope: No parent is selected or replaced. The earlier possible but ungraded John comparison is retained as history; 18% is a new individual assessment, not a numerical downgrade from an invented midpoint. No earlier wife, marriage, mother or birth date is supplied. The transcription’s first-marriage field is positive counterevidence, rather than simply an unrecorded earlier union. Robert’s original return records daughter Margaret aged 50 alongside a reported 1803 marriage, so two-year birth/marriage discrepancies occur in this household; that does not explain a twelve-year discrepancy for John. John’s exceptional age 99 also needs checking. John’s original page was not newly inspected; the detailed transcription and Robert’s held original were checked. This concerns the 1851 Glenleslie man only, and does not identify the Lisnagaver tithe occupier, validate attached descendants, propagate fatherhood to probable brother Hugh or establish a DNA pedigree.
